CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

zutempo implements the Temporal date and time model of ECMA-262 in R: Instant, ZonedDateTime, PlainDateTime, PlainDate, PlainTime, PlainYearMonth, PlainMonthDay, Duration and Now, in the ISO 8601 calendar, with IANA time zones read from the same database base R uses. The arithmetic is a transliteration of the specification’s abstract operations into C over the specification’s full ranges, so a result in R matches the result in a browser or in Node. It has no hard runtime dependency: zufast is LinkingTo only (header-only C, needed at build time). It does not do non-ISO calendars, locale formatting, custom time zones, strftime, or arithmetic operators in 0.1.0.

The specification is .agents/design.md and the plan is .agents/roadmap.md. They outrank this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides, the roadmap says what each stage builds and when it is done.

Current state

Verified 2026-10-15: stages 0 to 9. The eight types exist with every member of the pinned specification: fields, with*, compare, equals, round, add, subtract, since, until, total, startOfDay, getTimeZoneTransition, the conversions among the types and toString() with all its options; every Now function works; strings are read with every RFC 9557 annotation, and zutempo_parse() (R/parse.R) reads them in bulk with NA for failures. The ledger’s pending list is empty. The engine has the ISO records (src/ztp_iso.c), rounding (src/ztp_round.c), formatting (src/ztp_format.c), the parser with its goals, the annotation rules, the time zone and calendar string readers and the zufast fast path (src/ztp_parse.c), durations on 128-bit time durations (src/ztp_duration.c), calendar arithmetic with relative rounding with and without a zone and the zoned arithmetic (src/ztp_relative.c), instants with the UTC, fixed-offset and IANA zone kinds (src/ztp_instant.c) and the time zone database: TZif reader and footer rules (src/ztp_tz.c), the session cache (src/ztp_tz_cache.c) and the generated link table (src/ztp_tz_links.c); the glue is src/ztp_r_plain.c, src/ztp_r_duration.c, src/ztp_r_instant.c, src/ztp_r_tz.c and src/ztp_r_zoned.c (src/ztp_zoned.c holds the candidate search, disambiguation, start of day and the zoned string form). R/tz.R finds the database and reads the files; R/zoned-date-time.R is the zoned type. The oracle covers the eight types. See the roadmap’s stage table.

Stage tracking

Progress toward the next version is tracked as GitHub sub-issues, so the parent issue shows a progress bar such as “6 of 14”.

  • One parent issue per target version, titled with the bare version: v0.1.0 (#2).
  • One sub-issue per roadmap stage, titled as the roadmap titles it, for example Stage 2 — PlainDate, PlainTime and PlainDateTime, and linking to that section. The roadmap has fourteen stages, 0 to 13.
  • Every tracking issue carries the stage label, so it can be told apart from bug and feature issues and left out of open-issue counts.
  • Close a stage by merging its pull request. Put Closes #<n> in the body of the stage’s pull request. Never close a stage whose exit criteria are not met; record a deviation in the roadmap first.
  • The roadmap stays authoritative. The issues record which stages are done, not what a stage requires. Adding, removing or renaming a stage means editing the roadmap and the sub-issues in the same change.
  • Close the parent issue when CRAN accepts the version and it is tagged.

Versioning

The package develops at 0.0.0.9000 and targets 0.1.0 for its first CRAN release. Set Version: 0.1.0 and the matching NEWS.md heading when the package enters Pre-flight. Bump to 0.1.0.9000 only after CRAN accepts it, never before.

zutempo depends on zufast through LinkingTo and develops against its default branch (Remotes: pedrobtz/zufast) until zufast 0.1.1 is on CRAN; zutempo is not submitted before then (roadmap, open question 1). Nothing depends on zutempo yet. The C table for other packages (design §7) comes after 0.1.0.

Commands

Run from the package root.

Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'                # compile src/ and load
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                # roxygen -> NAMESPACE, man/
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                    # full testthat suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "<name>")'   # one test file
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE)'      # order independence
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                   # R CMD check
air format .                                     # format R sources

The default loop is document(), test(), check(). Before the first load_all(), install the development zufast: Rscript -e 'pak::pak("pedrobtz/zufast")'.

Occasional:

ZUTEMPO_CFLAGS=-DZUF_NO_INT128 Rscript -e 'devtools::clean_dll(); devtools::test()'
                                                 # the portable 128-bit build
Rscript tools/spec/members.R                     # regenerate inst/spec/members.csv
(cd tools/temporal-oracle && npm ci && npm run generate)
                                                 # regenerate tests/testthat/oracle/
(cd tools/temporal-oracle && npm run check-native)
                                                 # Node 26+: polyfill vs native

devtools::clean_dll() matters when ZUTEMPO_CFLAGS changes, and after any edit to a header that changes a struct’s layout: load_all() only recompiles .c files that changed, so an object built against the old header keeps the old sizes and the mismatch shows up as a stack smash (SIGABRT with no message) rather than a compile error.

Architecture

Design §4 is the reference. The layers, top down:

  • R/: argument and option normalisation, recycling, class and attribute handling, vctrs and pillar methods registered lazily.
  • src/ztp_r_*.c: the glue. R vectors in, column loops, NA handling, conditions raised with the 1-based index of the failing element.
  • src/ztp_*.c: the engine. The specification’s abstract operations over plain C structs, one C function per operation where practical, each commented with the section it implements. No SEXP, no R calls, no allocation in loops. Calendar algorithms and 128-bit intermediates come from zufast’s headers.
  • src/ztp_tz*.c: the zone cache. TZif reader and POSIX TZ footer rules (ztp_tz.c), the session cache keyed by case-folded identifier (ztp_tz_cache.c), the link table tools/tz/links.R generates (ztp_tz_links.c). The engine never touches the file system: R/tz.R finds the directory in base R’s order, walks it once per session for the identifier index, reads a zone’s bytes with readBin() and hands them to ztp_tz_cache_put(). ztp_zone_parse() only knows zones already in the cache, so every R entry point that takes a zone goes through ztp_tz_ensure() first.
  • tests/testthat/tzdata/: fat and slim TZif fixtures for 22 zones with the transitions zdump reports, from tools/tz/fixtures.R (needs zic and zdump). Regenerate when the tzdata pin moves.
  • src/init.c: the only exported symbol, R_init_zutempo. R reaches the registered routines as C_<name> (useDynLib(..., .fixes = "C_")).
  • A zoned_date_time() is the instant’s complex vector with the attribute zone (an integer code per element) and zones (the identifiers, in order of first use); new_zoned_date_time() recodes and drops unused identifiers, so build vectors through it or ztp_zoned_build(). Every engine call on zoned values goes through ztp_zdt_zones_ready(), which reloads the table’s zones: the C cache may have been cleared since the vector was made (a zutempo_tz_reset(), a change of database).
  • R/plumbing.R holds every base method that keeps the class through [, c(), rep(), unique(), printing and data frames: base R’s defaults drop the class attribute of a classed atomic vector. A new class needs each of them. R/zzz.R registers the vctrs and pillar methods lazily.
  • R/accessors.R is generated code in spirit: one generic, one default and one method per class for every Temporal property. The default finds the function the generic masks on the search path (lubridate::year()).
  • R/options.R turns option strings into the integer codes the glue reads; the enumerations in src/ztp_round.h and src/ztp_format.h fix the codes, so both sides change together.
  • src/ztp.h: ztp_status and ztp_ctx. An engine function takes a context and returns a status; on failure ztp_fail() records the status, the 1-based element index and a message. src/ztp_r.h: ztp_r_raise() turns a failed context into a condition by evaluating stop_zutempo() in the namespace.
  • tools/fuzz/: libFuzzer harnesses for the TZif reader, the RFC 9557 parser and the duration parser, run by hardening.yaml. Their seed corpora under tools/fuzz/corpus/ come from tools/fuzz/seeds.mjs (the oracle’s strings and test262’s); regenerate them when the oracle changes much.
  • inst/spec/PINS: the specification, test262 and tzdata pins (DCF). inst/spec/members.csv: every member of the pinned specification with its R name, written by tools/spec/members.R.
  • tools/temporal-oracle/: the Node project that writes tests/testthat/oracle/<Type>.json from temporal-polyfill. Cases are data in cases.js; expectations come from the engine.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • The engine never calls R. Errors are status codes plus a message in a per-call buffer; the glue turns them into conditions. This is what lets the same engine serve C callers after 0.1.0. An Rf_error() or an allocation inside ztp_*.c breaks that.
  • Values are stored exactly in R’s own vector types (design §4.1). No bit reinterpretation, no 64-bit integers smuggled in doubles. 128-bit integers exist only inside C.
  • Nanoseconds are normalised to [0, 1e9) with the floor convention, so lexicographic order on (Re, Im) of a complex value is chronological order.
  • Every TZif count and offset is bounds-checked against the file size before use. The reader is a fuzz target.
  • A slim TZif file needs the POSIX footer. R’s own database is slim; macOS’s is fat, which hides a footer bug on the developer’s machine (design §0).
  • Duration fields are doubles because Temporal’s are. Field-to-normalised conversion is a sum of products in 128 bits, never a double computation.
  • The pinned specification moves only on purpose. inst/spec/PINS records the tc39/proposal-temporal and test262 commits; changing either needs its own NEWS.md entry.
  • The suite must build and pass with ZUF_NO_INT128 as well as with __int128. CI runs both.
  • The pinned specification has two steps that cannot be followed literally (recorded in the roadmap under stage 4): ISODateSurpasses returns false when months is 0, which would leave CalendarDateUntil’s day loop without an exit, and ComputeNudgeWindow takes the origin when r1 is 0, which drops the larger units of the start duration. The engine does what the reference engines do; src/ztp_relative.c comments both places.
  • A list-backed class needs names() to return NULL. The fields are the list’s names; base R and vctrs read names() as element names, and rbind() and vec_c() break without the method. duration() is the example; ZonedDateTime will be the next.
  • Index lists with [[, never $. $ partial-matches names, so fields$month finds month_code when month is absent. This bit once in temporal_with().
  • An invalid option value is a zutempo_type_error (design 10), where JavaScript throws a RangeError; a value of the right kind that fails a range check (an increment that does not divide, a calendar other than ISO) is a zutempo_range_error. The oracle holds no invalid-option cases for that reason.

Testing conventions

  • Self-sufficient. Every test builds its own inputs inside the test_that() block. No file-scope objects.
  • Self-contained. Global state goes through withr::local_*(), randomised input through withr::local_seed(). Tests write only under tempdir().
  • Assert on condition classes, never message text. Use expect_error(..., class = "zutempo_<kind>_error"). Wording belongs in snapshot tests.
  • Order independence. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) is part of the definition of done.
  • Borrow a conformance suite before writing one. The oracle is temporal-polyfill under Node (tools/temporal-oracle/, from stage 1), checked against Node 26’s native Temporal; test262’s result assertions are translated in stage 11. Zone cases run against committed TZif fixtures from a pinned tzdata release, not the machine’s database.
  • Tests that need the machine’s database skip when it is missing.
  • Helpers live in tests/testthat/helper-*.R. helper-oracle.R reads an oracle JSON file (oracle_cases()) and holds one checker per type (oracle_check_plain_date(), …), which skips until that type’s constructor exists. test-oracle-<type>.R loops the cases through it.
  • test-members.R is the member ledger. When a stage exports a member, remove its name from pending there; the test fails otherwise.
  • Keep the long gctorture run inside its 120-minute budget. Its cost grows with the R code the tests run, not test blocks: an oracle file runs all its cases in one test_that() and compares fields in one expect_equal(). Under ZUTEMPO_GCTORTURE_SAMPLE=true the oracle runs one case per shape (oracle_gctorture_sample()), since a PROTECT bug is in the glue a shape reaches, not in the values; that cut the run by about 40% (2026-10-15). Add cases freely; add expectations with care. A heavy loop over values in another test file samples the same way.
  • Keep the suite inside the CRAN time budget. Not yet measured.

Definition of done

devtools::document() and devtools::check() clean, meaning 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes. The one allowed note is “New submission” before the first release. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) green. CI green on every leg of the quick run; the full run (full-ci) green once, before submission (see Continuous integration). A user-facing change also needs a test, roxygen documentation and a NEWS.md entry.

Releasing to CRAN

  • CI is the pre-submission check. The pedrobtz/r-actions R CMD check runs --as-cran on the CRAN-like runners and containers, and it replaces win-builder, the macOS builder and R-hub. None of them is a release step, and cran-comments.md lists the CI legs as its test environments.
  • Entering Pre-flight. The roadmap’s feature stages are done, the version is set as in Versioning, NEWS.md and cran-comments.md are written, and CI is green. Only submission work remains.
  • Before submitting, run the pkg-cran-review skill and resolve every finding.
  • The pretest is automated and does not read cran-comments.md. A NOTE that is explained but not fixed gets the upload archived. Fix the NOTE instead of justifying it.
  • After acceptance, tag v0.1.0, publish the GitHub release, bump to 0.1.0.9000, and close the version’s parent issue.

Editing rules

  • roxygen comments are the source. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Edit README.Rmd, not the generated README.md (from stage 12).
  • Keep prose simple and short. One idea per sentence. British spelling.
  • Wrap roxygen text at 80 characters and run air format . on R sources.
  • Use lower_snake_case. R names follow design §5: constructors named after the type, temporal_ for methods, accessors named after the property, now_ for Temporal.Now, zutempo_ for package helpers. Internal native symbols are prefixed ztp_; the public C prefix is zutempo_.
  • Keep hard runtime dependencies at zero. zufast is LinkingTo only.
  • Export and document public functions. Do not create roxygen topics for internal ones.

Continuous integration

Workflows come from pedrobtz/r-actions. Call those reusable workflows instead of writing bespoke ones, and pin a released tag rather than main. Pin a workflow that holds a write token, such as coverage.yml, to a commit, with the tag in a comment. The R-CMD-check workflow must call r-cmd-check.yml, because a hand-rolled one does not count as the pre-submission check.

Every run is the quick one: each job finishes in under five minutes, on pull requests and on pushes to main alike. The full run, the slow jobs at their full length, happens once, before submission (roadmap stage 13): put the full-ci label on the release pull request and run gh workflow run gctorture.yaml if the long gctorture is wanted alone. A finding of the full run is fixed then. Do not add full-ci to an ordinary pull request.

This package calls:

  • R-CMD-check.yaml: r-cmd-check.yml@v1, quick on pull requests, full on main or with the full-ci label.
  • R-CMD-check.yaml also runs R-CMD-check-no-int128, the same check with ZUTEMPO_CFLAGS=-DZUF_NO_INT128 in the environment, which src/Makevars adds to PKG_CFLAGS; test-info.R asserts that the flag reached the engine.
  • native-checks.yml: sanitizers.yml (UBSan and ASan), lto.yml, rchk.yml (with github-packages: pedrobtz/zufast, since the rchk image ignores Remotes:), analyzers.yml and cran-special.yml in full on every run, two or three minutes each; valgrind.yml (about eleven minutes) only with full-ci; gctorture.yml at step 1000 over the sampled oracle, and at step 20 (about an hour) with full-ci or the gctorture label.
  • gctorture.yaml: the long gctorture run alone, on demand (gh workflow run gctorture.yaml).
  • coverage.yaml: coverage.yml pinned to a commit. The badge is committed to gh-pages because main takes no direct pushes.
  • pkgdown.yaml: the r-lib site build, deploying to gh-pages with force: false so it does not overwrite the badge.
  • hardening.yaml: fuzz.yml three times, one job per harness under tools/fuzz/ (TZif, RFC 9557, duration), against the engine sources (the glue excluded). The TZif job is seeded from the slim fixtures, the others from tools/fuzz/corpus/; two minutes each on a pull request and a push to main, thirty with full-ci or on demand (gh workflow run hardening.yaml), with the corpus carried between runs. The harnesses build without R: Homebrew’s clang -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined over src/ztp_*.c minus src/ztp_r_*.c with zufast’s headers is the local smoke test (Apple’s clang has no libFuzzer). The engine’s strings are length-delimited, so never print one with a plain %s.

Small edits get a small run. The shared workflows look at the files a pull request changes, compared with its merge base:

  • Markdown only, such as README.md, NEWS.md or cran-comments.md, skips every check. Only coverage and the pkgdown site run.
  • DESCRIPTION or README.Rmd as well, and nothing else, adds one R CMD check on Ubuntu R-release.
  • Any other file runs everything.

So put a README or DESCRIPTION touch-up in its own pull request. Once a pull request changes code, every later push to it runs in full.

Commits and pull requests

Short, imperative, sentence-case commit subjects, optionally scoped. Keep each commit focused and do not sweep in unrelated files. A pull request explains the user-visible outcome and the rationale, links related issues, lists the checks that were run and the tests that were skipped, and flags platform-sensitive changes. Performance claims need evidence.

Never commit or push to the default branch. Work on a branch, open a pull request, and merge it only when every check is green. A stage’s pull request closes its sub-issue.

When you find a defect, in this package or in an upstream tool, open an issue for it rather than only working around it.
